haiku-low.q1: After the message and its outbox row commit (steps 1-4), the sender gets ack(msg_id, seq). It does not wait for recipients.
haiku-low.q2: Sender gets an error; nothing is stored or delivered. Retry reuses the same msg_id, which the Store enforces as unique, so no second copy.
haiku-low.q3: 30 seconds after its last heartbeat; heartbeats arrive every 10 seconds, and the Presence entry expires via TTL.
haiku-low.q4: The Inbox entry stays, the recipient counts as offline for that message, and a push is sent. A late ack still deletes it.
haiku-low.q5: The failure is logged and not retried. Push never touches the Inbox or Store, so the message still waits for reconnect.
haiku-low.q6: Reconnect delivers Inbox-listed messages in seq order per conversation. Duplicates are dropped by the client using msg_id.
haiku-low.q7: The message and its outbox row are committed in one transaction, and the Relay publishes unpublished rows on recovery, so it is never lost.
haiku-low.q8: Presence Registry maps user id to gateway. Its entry expires by TTL, 30 s after the last heartbeat, which removes dead connections.
haiku-low.q9: The worker sends it through the recipient's gateway to their client; a client ack within 5 s confirms arrival, and the Inbox entry is then deleted.
haiku-low.q10: The per-user Offline Inbox. The worker writes an entry first, before delivery is tried. Entries are deleted on client ack or after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The user's Offline Inbox entries (msg_id, conversation id, seq), then the message bodies fetched from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: Its bus offset is uncommitted, so another worker reprocesses the event. Inbox writes are keyed by (user, msg_id), so repeats are harmless; duplicates are possible.

sonnet.q1: Only after the Message Store transaction (message + outbox row) commits. The ack(msg_id, seq) tells the sender the message is durably stored with that seq; no recipient is involved yet.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No message or outbox row exists, so nobody receives it. The retry must carry the same msg_id (Store enforces unique msg_id, so no second copy).
sonnet.q3: After 30 seconds without a heartbeat (heartbeats are sent every 10 s); the Presence entry expires by TTL.
sonnet.q4: The Inbox entry stays, the recipient is treated as offline for that message, and the worker sends a push (one attempt). A late ack still deletes the entry; if the client reconnects first it may get the message again and drops the duplicate by msg_id.
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged and not retried. Push never touches the Inbox or Store, so the message still waits for the recipient at reconnect.
sonnet.q6: In seq order per conversation. Duplicates are dropped by the client using msg_id (clients keep seen message ids).
sonnet.q7: The message and its outbox row are written in one transaction, so the outbox row exists once committed. The Outbox Relay publishes unpublished rows to the Event Bus on recovery, so an acknowledged message is never lost (a possible double publish is just a duplicate clients drop).
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry (user id to gateway). Each heartbeat refreshes the entry and it expires by TTL 30 s after the last heartbeat, which removes it.
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker looks up the recipient in the Presence Registry, sends the message via the recipient's Gateway (Gateway B) to the client. The client's ack, which must arrive within 5 s, confirms it, and then the Inbox entry is deleted.
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox (per-user; entries hold msg_id, conversation id, seq, not the body). Written by the worker for each recipient before attempting delivery. Removed when the client acks (live ack or reconnect ack); otherwise expires after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: The gateway reads that user's entries from the Offline Inbox, then fetches the message bodies from the Message Store, and sends them in seq order per conversation.
sonnet.q12: The bus offset was not committed, so another worker receives the event again and redoes it. Inbox writes are keyed by (user, msg_id) so repeats are harmless; some recipients may get the message or a push twice, and clients drop duplicate messages by msg_id.
